additions.source_quote: עַד בֹּא הַשָּׁמֶשׁ – הַיְנוּ לְהַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁל הַדָּבָר
additions.justification: The text makes an explicit second bechina beyond the one captured in the dataset: 'until the sun came — that is, [until reaching] the sekhel of the matter.' This is an interpretation of the verse (Exodus 17:12) that directly equates שמש (sun) with שכל (intellect/sekhel). The phrasing 'הַיְנוּ לְהַשֵּׂכֶל' (i.e., to the sekhel) is Rebbe Nachman's standard bechina language: the verse-word IS the concept. This creates a second bechina pair: שמש ↔ שכל, which would connect שכל into the existing package alongside שמש ↔ חכמה. Since שכל and חכמה are near-synonyms in Rebbe Nachman's usage (as shown throughout Likutay Moharan, e.g. Torah #1, #4), this addition would extend Package 1 to three nodes: שמש ↔ חכמה ↔ שכל — all three expressing the same illuminating, wisdom-dimension reality. The dataset currently records שכל only in eitza relation to this Torah (אמונה → שכל, edge 2889, type=eitza, ref=91) — the bechina identity שמש = שכל is not captured as a separate bechina edge.

additions.package_label: אֱמוּנָה — Faith Embodied in the Limbs
additions.source_quote: וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה – שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ אֱמוּנָה כָּל כָּךְ גְּדוֹלָה, עַד שֶׁנִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל הָאֵיבָרִים, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בְּיָדָיו הָיָה הָאֱמוּנָה כָּל כָּךְ גְּדוֹלָה
additions.justification: The verse 'וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה' (and his hands were faith) is interpreted as a bechina equation: Moses's ידים (hands) = אמונה (faith). The Rebbe explains that Moses had faith so great it spread through all his limbs — 'even in his hands the faith was so great.' This is the paradimatic illustration of the Torah's opening principle: true faith (אמונה) does not remain only in the heart but spreads into the body's limbs, becoming embodied faith. The hands here ARE faith — they are not merely the instrument of faith but its bechina expression. This bechina pair (ידים ↔ אמונה) is not present in the dataset for Torah #91. It would form the foundation of a second package centered on אמונה (the dominant theme of the Torah), which would group: אמונה, ידים, אֵיבָרִים (the limbs into which faith spreads), and possibly לב (the heart — the basic minimal location of simple faith, contrasted with full-body embodied faith). See analysis_notes for the proposed package structure.

additions.package_label: אֱמוּנָה — Faith Embodied in the Limbs
additions.source_quote: וְהָעִקָּר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לָאָדָם אֱמוּנָה כָּל־כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל הָאֵיבָרִים
additions.justification: The text states that the ideal state of faith is that 'it spreads through all the limbs (אֵיבָרִים).' The Rebbe does not say that faith causes the limbs to act — he says it spreads INTO them, so that the limbs become the embodiment of faith. The limbs (אֵיבָרִים) are thus a bechina expression of embodied faith: they ARE faith when faith is at its fullest. This is confirmed by the proof from Moses: 'וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה' — his hands (= his limbs) WERE faith. The pair אמונה ↔ איברים would belong in a second package (see analysis_notes below) as a bechina of the same embodied-faith domain.

additions.package_label: אֱמוּנָה — Faith Embodied in the Limbs
additions.source_quote: כִּי בְּלֹא אֱמוּנָה אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תהילים קי"ט): כָּל מִצְו‍ֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה
additions.justification: The verse 'כָּל מִצְו‍ֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה' (all Your commandments are faith — Psalms 119:86) is cited to prove that without faith, a mitzvah is nothing. This is a classic bechina citation in Rebbe Nachman's style: the verse equates מצוות with אמונה (all commandments = faith). The physical mitzvot — including raising the hands during netilah — are expressions of embodied faith in action. The pair מצוות ↔ אמונה would extend Package 2 as a further bechina of embodied practical faith.

proposed_second_package.label: אֱמוּנָה — Faith Embodied in the Limbs
proposed_second_package.label_en: Emunah: Faith That Spreads Through the Body
proposed_second_package.reason: The entire Torah #91 is about אמונה (faith) — yet אמונה does not appear as a node in any bechina edge for Torah #91 in the current dataset. This is the most significant gap. The Torah teaches that: (1) faith exists in different modes — basic faith (in the heart only) versus fully embodied faith (which spreads through all the limbs); (2) the embodiment of faith is expressed through physical acts like raising the hands during netilat yadayim; (3) Moses's hands being called 'faith' ('יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה') is the paradigmatic illustration. The implicit bechina network here is: אמונה ↔ ידים ↔ איברים ↔ מצוות — all four share the essential nature of 'faith expressed in bodily action.' If these bechina edges were added, they would form a second package (Package 2) that is the thematic heart of the Torah. Package 2's eitza connection to Package 1: the embodied faith (אמונה, ידים, איברים) leads →eitza→ to the sun of wisdom (שמש, חכמה, שכל). This is precisely the eitza edge already in the dataset (edge 2889, ref=91, type=eitza): 'when one has this kind of faith, one comes from faith to sekhel.' The good/evil mirror is absent from Torah #91 — the teaching has no evil-side discussion, making it exclusively a positive teaching with no klipah counterpart.
proposed_second_package.note: This proposed second package has 4 candidate concepts, all drawn from explicit bechina language in the source text. It meets the threshold of 3+ concepts. See torah_91_new_packages.json for the formal new-package assessment.

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_analysis: Torah #91 has no evil-side discussion. It is a short, purely positive teaching about the virtue of embodied faith and its elevation to wisdom. There is no discussion of a negative counterforce, no klipah mirror, no opposing concept. This is not unusual for very short teachings in Likutay Moharan that function as short homiletical observations rather than full structural teachings.
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: אמונה — the central concept of the entire Torah; appears only in an eitza edge (ref=91, type=eitza: 'when one has this kind of faith → sekhel') but not as a bechina node for Torah #91
ידים — 'יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה' interprets Moses's hands as the bechina/expression of faith; appears as a bechina node in Torah #80 (ידים ↔ חכמה) but NOT for Torah #91
איברים — the limbs that faith spreads into and becomes embodied in; no bechina edge in the dataset for Torah #91
מצוות — 'כָּל מִצְו‍ֹתֶיךָ אֱמוּנָה' equates all commandments with faith; cited as proof text but not as a bechina node for Torah #91
שכל — the sun (שמש) is glossed as 'הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁל הַדָּבָר' (the sekhel of the matter); a second bechina of שמש beyond the חכמה one; not in dataset for Torah #91

לב — 'יֵשׁ אֱמוּנָה שֶׁהוּא רַק בַּלֵּב' (faith that is only in the heart) — the heart is the baseline location of simple faith, implicitly contrasted with the ideal of faith-in-all-limbs; not present as a bechina node for Torah #91
משה — the paradigmatic example of embodied faith ('יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה'); not a bechina node for Torah #91 in the dataset
נטילת ידים — the act of raising hands during hand-washing is cited as the physical expression requiring embodied faith; an eitza context but grounded in a bechina (hands = faith)
analysis_notes.note_on_torah_length: Torah #91 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan vol. 1 — just 7 lines. Its brevity explains the minimal bechina footprint in the dataset (1 explicit bechina edge). The entire structural depth of the teaching resides in the eitza dimension (faith → sekhel) supported by one foundational bechina (sun = wisdom). More faithful encoding would add at minimum 3-4 additional bechina edges to capture the faith-embodiment cluster.
